About us

We provide independent advice to the New Zealand Government on mitigating climate change and adapting to its impacts, and we monitor and report on the Government's progress towards its climate goals. We're online 9am–5pm, Monday–Friday.

    A huge milestone today – the Commission delivered its second biennial adaptation progress assessment to the Minister this morning. This latest progress report provides an updated assessment of the implementation and effectiveness of the Government’s national adaptation planning, with advice and recommendations for action. We also delivered a companion report, which contains information on exposure and vulnerability to select climate-related hazards at a national level, relevant for national adaptation planning. It’s now over to the Minister of Climate Change to present our assessment report to Parliament. We will publish it on our website once it has been tabled in the House – watch this space! While leading this work has been my main focus for the last while, these projects have drawn on the time, skills and expertise of many wonderful Commission staff at different stages over the last many months, often alongside other pressing priorities. It was great to grab a moment ahead of delivery to mark the occasion with a picture! #ClimateChange | #ClimateAdaptation | #NAPPA | #ClimateAction

    Every significant transition involves trade-offs. The question is whether we confront them early and deliberately - or leave them to become larger, more expensive problems later. That's one of the clearest messages from our latest emissions monitoring report, released this week: https://lnkd.in/eAGYEGn5 New Zealand needs to accelerate the pace of emissions reductions. Our assessment shows current policy settings are not delivering reductions at the rate needed, and decisions made in the next 12-24 months will matter most. None of the choices ahead are cost-free. Investing in new technology requires capital. Building infrastructure takes time. Changing systems always creates uncertainty. But delaying decisions has costs too. Households remain exposed to energy price shocks. Businesses miss opportunities to improve productivity and reduce operating costs. Future governments inherit fewer options and greater pressure to act quickly. What struck me most in this year's assessment is that many of the opportunities are no longer theoretical. Technologies that reduce emissions are increasingly delivering practical benefits today - lower running costs, greater resilience and reduced exposure to future risks. Yet upfront costs, uncertainty and other barriers continue to slow their uptake. Our report also found that the government has low-cost options for addressing those barriers: targeted funding and financing mechanisms, stable investment signals for markets and consumers, and better information to support household and business decisions. This is not really a choice between affordability and reducing emissions. It's a question of which costs, risks and opportunities we choose to carry forward. The countries that navigate this transition most successfully are unlikely to be those that avoid difficult decisions altogether. They will be the ones that make them early enough to keep their options open. #ClimateChange | #EmissionsReduction

    We're all about the win-wins and, as our research has shown, going electric saves money and reduces emissions. The electrification tipping point was reached in 2024 and the gap between fossil fuelled homes and electric homes doubling in two years. The Climate Change Commission's latest report backs that up and advocates for policies that will not only help address the rising cost of living, but also get us back on track to meet our climate obligations. These two things are not mutually exclusive and the CCC suggests the Government needs to do more to help homes upgrade, offer more help for businesses to electrify and focus on policies that will increase EV adoption, with a particular focus on low-income homes. Read the story on Newsroom here ⚡https://lnkd.in/ein2un9m

    Some of New Zealand's greatest economic opportunities may also be its biggest climate opportunities. Across households and businesses, many low-emissions technologies are no longer future solutions. They are available today, and in many cases already make financial sense: - EVs are cheaper to run than petrol vehicles, and upfront costs have dropped. For comparable compact SUVs, EV owners can save about NZ$7,500 in running costs over five years. - In parts of Australia (where about a third of households have solar), rooftop solar and battery systems are helping reduce regulated electricity prices by up to 10%. - It’s now generally cheaper for businesses to buy and run a new industrial heat pump than continue running an existing fossil-fuel low-temperature boiler. Yet uptake remains slower than it could be. Our new monitoring report [ https://lnkd.in/eBGJk4ZC ] suggests that the challenge is increasingly less about technology and more about barriers - upfront costs, uncertainty, financing and information. Every year these barriers remain in place is another year that households and businesses miss out on savings, resilience and greater protection from future energy shocks. Climate action is often framed as a cost. The evidence increasingly points to a different story: done well, it can help create a more productive, resilient and competitive economy These images I've posted here show some of the findings in our 2026 emissions reduction monitoring report - you can find the whole report and a range of different supporting material on our website: https://lnkd.in/eBGJk4ZC -- Images: 1 - Five year running costs of compact SUVs - battery EVs versus petrol cars. 2- Cost of installing and running *new* heat pumps versus running *existing* fossil fuel boilers (coal, gas, diesel, LPG). [Our assessment of the business case for these is available on our website in the technical documents alongside the main report.] 3 - Actions with clear benefits for households and businesses to adopt now. There are so many opportunities that reduce both costs and emissions. -- #ClimateChange | #ClimateAction | #EmissionsReduction | #ClimateMitigation

    The next few years will shape New Zealand's options for decades. That's the central message of our latest emissions monitoring report, out today: https://lnkd.in/eBGJk4ZC The encouraging news is that emissions have been falling. The challenging news is that progress stalled in 2024. The rate of reduction now needs to more than double if New Zealand is to remain on track for its climate goals. Current policy settings are not delivering at the pace needed. What makes this moment important is that in many cases, the solutions we need - the technologies, investments and policy tools - already exist. What matters now is timing. Our assessment shows there is still an opportunity to change course, but that window is narrowing. Decisions made over the next 12-24 months will have an outsized influence on whether New Zealand can manage future risks, strengthen resilience and keep more options open for the future. There is still an opportunity to shape the transition. The sooner New Zealand acts, the more options it has to achieve a well-paced, resilient and affordable transition. #ClimateChange
